column1: # boru Language Specification: Higher-order list words (each fold scan join)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# each / fold / scan take an unevaluated CODE BODY (NoEvalArgs) as their
# first argument and a collection as the second; the body runs against
# each element on the stack. fold optionally takes an initial accumulator;
# scan has no init form — it always seeds from the first element. (filter,
# which takes a Function callback, and the richer combinators —
# where/group/unique/sortby — live in the boru:array-util module.)
# §1  each — map a code body over a list
each [mul 2] [1 2 3]
column3: double each element
increment each element

column1: each [dup add] [1 2 3]
column3: the body may use stack ops

column1: [1 2 3] each [mul 2]
column3: mixed split (collection on the stack)

column1: # §2  fold — reduce a list with a binary body
fold [add] [1 2 3 4] 0
column3: sum with explicit initial accumulator

column1: fold [add] [1 2 3 4]
column3: no-init form folds from the first element

column1: fold [mul] [1 2 3 4] 1
column3: product

column1: # §3  scan — running (prefix) reduction
scan [add] [1 2 3]
column3: running sums

column1: scan [mul] [1 2 3 4]
column3: running products

column1: scan [add] [42]
column3: a singleton is just its seed (scan has no init form)

column1: scan [add] []
column3: empty in, empty out

column1: # §4  join — concatenate list elements into a String

column3: join with a separator

column1: join ['a' 'b' 'c']
column3: default separator is a comma

column1: # §6  LIST Function form for each / for-each / fold / scan (NUR086's fix,
#     2026-08-24). The callback receives the ELEMENT — the container's
#     natural unit — so a plain `Integer -> Integer` function value can be
#     handed to an iterator directly, no quotation wrapper and no adapter
#     lambda. THE FAMILY RULE: a PER-CONTAINER Function form hands the
#     container's natural unit (element for a list, KeyVal for a map);
#     `filter`'s single cross-container form (§5) is the documented
#     exception — one signature serving both shapes, so it hands a POSITION
#     descriptor either way. See REFERENCE.md §"Higher-order array words".
#     GRADUATED 2026-08-27 (Stage 3): the list `each` rows below moved
#     here out of lang/spec/frontier/frontier-hof-audit.tsv §12, where
#     they sat because the compile lane reached the callback through an
#     ISLAND. lambdaCallbackInputs simply had no list case for `each` —
#     it handled the MAP twin and fell through — so the lambda lowering
#     declined at its first gate. The convention was measured off the
#     interpreter rather than inferred from the map twin:
#     `def show fn [[e:Any][Any][typeof e]] each show/v [1 2 3]` answers
#     [Integer Integer Integer], i.e. ONE input, the bare element, passed
#     through unchanged. fold / scan / for-each still island — their
#     conventions carry an ACCUMULATOR whose type after step 1 is the
#     body's return, which is a separate measured question.
def dbl x:Integer => [mul 2 x]  each dbl/v [1 2 3]
column3: a Function VALUE maps over a list — the element reaches the callback with no quotation wrapper

column1: def dbl x:Integer => [mul 2 x]  each [dbl] [1 2 3]
column3: …and the quotation wrapper it replaces still answers identically

column1: each ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) [1]
column3: a LAMBDA over a LIST is an each signature since NUR086's fix — neither a quotation wrapper nor a map form is needed

column1: each ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) [1 2 3]
column3: …over more than one element, the closure body is compiled ONCE and driven per element

column1: each ([x:Any] => [typeof x]) [1 'a' true]
column3: a HETEROGENEOUS list: the element carrier is the lattice join, so the body dispatches per alternative exactly as the runtime does

column1: each ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) []
column3: the empty list runs the callback zero times

column1: def n 3  each ([x:Integer] => [x mul n]) [1 2]
column3: the callback CAPTURES an enclosing binding — the capture rides the closure, not a re-lookup

column1: def kf kv:KeyVal => [mul 2 (kv.v)]  each kf/v {a:1 b:2}
column3: the MAP form is unchanged: a per-container form hands a KeyVal

column1: # §5  filter — keep elements whose callback returns true. The callback is
#     a Function (not a code body). Over a LIST it receives a {key value}
#     pair map (key = index); read the element via `.value`. Over a MAP it
#     receives a KeyVal {k v i n} (read the value via `.v`) and the result
#     keeps the map shape. The afn param must be typed, e.g. [kv:KeyVal].
filter ([p:Any] => [(p.value mod 2) eq 0]) [1 2 3 4 5 6]
column3: keep even elements (pair.value)

column1: filter ([p:Any] => [p.value gt 3]) [1 2 3 4 5]
column3: keep elements greater than 3

column1: filter ([kv:KeyVal] => [(kv.v mod 2) eq 0]) {a:1 b:2 c:3 d:4}
column3: map: keeps entries by value, returns a map; the lambda gets a KeyVal

column1: # §5b filter quotation form — like each/fold, a [body] runs once per
#     element with the ELEMENT pushed first (no {key value} wrapper).
#     Keeps the elements whose body result is Boolean true; a
#     non-Boolean body result is a loud error (DX report T9.2).
filter [2 gt] [1 2 3 4]
column3: quotation form: keep elements greater than 2

column1: [1 2 3 4] [2 gt] filter
column3: quotation form, stack form

column1: filter [mod 2 eq 0] [1 2 3 4 5 6]
column3: quotation form: keep even elements

column1: filter [2 gt] {a:1 b:5 c:3}
column3: quotation form on a map filters by value, keeping a map

column1: filter [add 1] [1 2 3]
column3: a body that yields a non-Boolean is a loud error, not a silent drop

column1: # §6  errors
each [mul 2] 5
column3: each requires a list collection

column1: fold [add] 5 0
column3: fold requires a list collection

column1: # §7  map forms — each / for-each / fold / filter over a map. The quotation
#     form gets the VALUE (key preserved); the lambda form gets a KeyVal
#     {k v i n}. each/filter keep the map shape; fold reduces. keys/vals
#     (map.tsv) project a map to a list.
{a:1 b:2 c:3} each [mul 10]
column3: each over a map: quotation transforms values, keeps keys

column1: each [mul 10] {a:1 b:2}
column3: forward form

column1: {a:1 b:2} each ([kv:KeyVal] => [kv.v add kv.i])
column3: each lambda receives a KeyVal (value + iteration index)

column1: {a:1 b:5 c:3} filter ([kv:KeyVal] => [kv.v gt 2])
column3: filter lambda receives a KeyVal, keeps the map shape

column1: fold [add] {a:1 b:2 c:3} 0
column3: fold over a map sums the values (explicit seed)

column1: fold [add] {a:10 b:20 c:5}
column3: no-init form folds from the first value

column1: 0 fold ([acc:Integer kv:KeyVal] => [acc add kv.v]) {a:1 b:2 c:3}
column3: fold lambda receives (accumulator, KeyVal)

column1: {a:1} each [drop]
column3: a map each body that produces nothing is an error

column1: {a:1 b:5} filter ([kv:KeyVal] => [kv.v])
column3: a non-Boolean map predicate is a loud error

column1: fold [add] {}
column3: empty map with no initial value is an error

column1: # §8  scan over a map — running fold over the values, keeping the keys
{a:1 b:2 c:3} scan [add]
column3: scan over a map: running fold over the values, keeps keys

column1: {a:1 b:2 c:3} scan ([acc:Integer kv:KeyVal] => [acc add kv.v])
column3: scan lambda gets (accumulator, KeyVal)

column1: {a:5} scan [add]
column3: a singleton map is its seed

column1: {a:1 b:2} scan [drop drop]
column3: a scan body that leaves nothing is an error
